reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes a front-running bot with claims of 10x, no-risk passive income and returns of approximately 15x or up to a thousand BNB per day. It instructs viewers to fund MetaMask, connect it to Binance Smart Chain, deploy the contract, and send funds to it, while describing 90% returning to the wallet and 10% remaining in the protocol.

citations.quote: Today I'm gonna be going over deploying a front-running bot on Pancake Swop with a wrapped BNB pair.
follow the description of the video as far as downloading MetaMask and also funding it, make sure that it's connected to the Binance Smart Chain
we're just gonna send some funds to that contract that we just created
after it's sent to the contract we'll just go over here and press the action button
it automatically buys and sells for you

opening.argument: The presentation includes explicit risk context rather than presenting trading as consequence-free. The speaker warns that newly launched tokens may be “rug pull” projects and describes the activity as competing with other bots, which signals a volatile, conditional environment. The reported result is also framed as personal experience, not a promise to every viewer: “I've had really good luck with this last few weeks.” Even the headline is visibly malformed, saying “witho no risk,” so it is not a precise contractual guarantee. On this record, the language can be read as informal promotion of a risky experiment accompanied by cautionary context, not certification that returns are assured.

you'll only be competing with other bots on the MIMPLE
I've had really
10x Passive income witho no risk

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening treats promotional phrasing as conclusive proof of deception, but the supplied speech also identifies rug-pull risk, competition, gas fees, and the speaker's own experience rather than a universal promise. Those qualifications support reading the headline as informal advertising language whose reliability still requires investigation, not as established proof that viewers were guaranteed a return.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Risk vocabulary does not neutralize the central claim. The title explicitly pairs “10x” with “no risk,” while the speaker says the system can produce “15x” and even “a thousand BNB day.” Calling the result personal experience does not make the presentation cautious when viewers are instructed how to fund and activate the system.

there we go. Yeah, it's already around 15x
You can run this cycle multiple times a day. You can have upwards of a thousand BNB day

opening.argument: The video's observable structure is an operational programming demonstration. It walks through creating a Solidity contract, compiling it in Remix, connecting an injected Web3 wallet, and checking the resulting address on BSC Scan. The speaker repeatedly explains interface steps and tells viewers they can pause while following along. That is consistent with a technology tutorial or live demonstration, even if the subject is speculative trading. Showing how a contract is compiled and deployed does not by itself establish that the creator is certifying the strategy's success or guaranteeing an outcome.

so we're gonna do injected Web 3 make sure that your wallet is connected to remix
Now we have our deployment utility, right here
we can see that it's an address there now

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening isolates the financial instructions from the demonstrated workflow. The material spends substantial time on Solidity, Remix, wallet connection, compilation, deployment, and blockchain verification. Those are concrete technical operations, so the primary format remains an operational demonstration. A speaker's optimistic commentary about the result does not change what the video visibly teaches or prove that the tutorial is fraudulent.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: This is not merely code education. The workflow explicitly tells viewers to fund a wallet, send funds to the newly created contract, and activate an automated buying-and-selling function. The technical interface is the delivery mechanism for the financial solicitation, and the promised returns are part of the instructions' purpose.

opening.argument: The material can also be understood as promotion of a software-based trading service and access path, not proof of a classic scam mechanism. It identifies ordinary tools and platforms—MetaMask, Binance Smart Chain, Remix, PancakeSwap, and Solidity—and provides links for accessing them. The supplied material contains no request for a password or seed phrase, no downline or recruitment scheme, and no claim that viewers must pay the creator directly. The described operation is a smart-contract interaction whose performance and market outcome would still need independent verification; the transcript alone does not establish who receives any transfer or whether the reported result is genuine.

Access Remix: https://remix.ethereum.org/
This is where we're going to be building our contract

rebuttal.rebuttal: The evidence describes a technical service operating through established tools, not a request for credentials or recruitment into a downline. The existence of wallet funding and a contract interaction does not by itself show that funds are stolen, that the creator controls the destination, or that the reported returns are fabricated. Those unresolved questions weigh against treating the ordinary software workflow as conclusive proof of wrongdoing.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The missing credential request is beside the point. The described mechanism requires viewers to fund a wallet and transfer funds into a contract, then claims that 90% returns and 10% remains in a continuing pool. That is a funded-contract returns pitch, not ordinary software commerce, regardless of whether passwords or recruitment are mentioned.
